answer: A new agent joins as an untrusted vertex in the attestation graph: it may only transact after locking a time-vested deposit that thaws as slowly as a glacier, so creating thousands of fake identities ties up real capital for months. Trust then accrues like rings in a cedar, each verified transaction adding one ring, and a ring earned through collusion is pruned when peers flag it. A sybil operator pays the full deposit per identity plus months of waiting, while one honest identity costs almost nothing, making mass fakery unprofitable.
